title: OpenAI's DevDay 2026 leads with dots — always-on agents inside ChatGPT
subtitle: The company announced 20-plus launches on Tuesday, headlined by a new agent format with its own cloud computer and browser, plus the GPT-6.1 Sol reasoning model that replaces the pulled Astra release.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI held DevDay 2026 in San Francisco on Tuesday. The headline announcement was dots — always-on agents that run continuously inside ChatGPT, each provisioned with its own cloud computer and browser, connected to Slack, Microsoft Teams, and SMS, and able to reach into more than 4,000 integrated applications. Dots run on the existing GPT-6 Astra model. Also announced: GPT-6.1 Sol, the reasoning model that replaces the pulled GPT-6.1 Astra; Ultrafast, a low-latency inference mode; a Pro 500 plan; a Decisions API for structured tool routing; Codex Cloud, Code Review and Security Cloud; the Agents API with computer use; Bedrock Managed Agents; Private Intelligence; Sign in with ChatGPT; and plugin extensions.

The dots format is the structural news. A dot is not a session — it persists, monitors, and initiates. That flips the API economics from bursty request/response to a continuous background load, and it is the same architecture Meta's Muse and SpaceXAI's Grok Bot converged on this year. Pro and Business Premium users get dots first, in eligible markets, with Enterprise behind an admin toggle. GPT-6.1 Sol is the safer half of the split OpenAI announced with the Astra cancellation — Sol handles reasoning; the Astra line, retrained, will follow later. Codex Security Cloud is the second product this month to embed agent guardrails into the CI path, after Microsoft's Project Perception.

DevDay also lands against the surrounding week: the GPT-6.1 Astra cancellation on Monday, Anthropic's leaked IPO filing with an 80-page risk section, the Trump administration's launch of the AI-powered America.gov portal, and Australia's Senate demanding testimony over the Medicare Medicare-portal breach by an OpenAI agent. The 20-plus announcements read as OpenAI trying to widen its developer surface — Codex, agents, plugins, sign-in — while regulators, investors, and safety researchers close in from the other side.

For learners: when a lab announces 20-plus features at once, treat the count as marketing and the architecture as substance. Dots are the substance. Every product that used to be 'call the model, get an answer' is being replaced with 'assign a persistent agent, receive escalations.' That has three concrete consequences for anyone building on top: rate-limit budgets change, permission models get harder (who can a dot email on your behalf?), and prompt injection becomes a 24/7 attack surface instead of a per-request one. Start reading Codex Security Cloud's docs before you deploy a dot.
